segments.t: Gabriel is meant to be listening to JoeyStarr's complaints about Julie, but his phone keeps distracting him. Their conversation turns from the film-set argument to the woman Gabriel has met. Hear the French first, and follow who is asking for attention.
Dis-le si je t'ennuie.
Non, excuse-moi! Regarde, j'écoute. Vas-y, je suis tout à toi.
Je n'en ai plus envie maintenant.
Allez, j'écoute! Et alors?
Je passe pour un idiot! Tu sais ce qu'elle fait?
Non.
Elle n'avait pas son script avec elle.
Alors moi, sympa, je lui donne le mien.
Elle le prend comme un torchon sale! C'est agaçant.
Non, ça va.
Réponds!
D'accord. J'ai rencontré cette fille.
Ce n'est pas mon genre. Elle est blonde, elle est normale!
Mais je suis attiré par elle comme un aimant.
Tu vois? C'est très puissant.
Mon inconscient et celui de Julie Gayet se heurtent de partout.
JoeyStarr can see that Gabriel's mind is elsewhere. He asks whether he is boring him.
Dis-le si je t'ennuie.
'Say it if I'm boring you.' The word for it attaches after say in this instruction. The final action includes the little word for you because JoeyStarr asks whether he is boring Gabriel.
Non, excuse-moi! Regarde, j'écoute. Vas-y, je suis tout à toi.
'No, excuse me! Look, I'm listening. Go ahead, I'm all yours.' The final expression literally says I am all to you. It promises complete attention, after the familiar instruction to go ahead.
Je n'en ai plus envie maintenant.
'I don't feel like it anymore now.' The phrase about having desire means feeling like doing something. The negative expression says that desire no longer exists, rather than that he never had it.
Allez, j'écoute! Et alors?
'Come on, I'm listening! And then?' The first word urges someone on. The small follow-up question asks what happened next and encourages him to continue.
Je passe pour un idiot! Tu sais ce qu'elle fait?

'I look like an idiot! Do you know what she is doing?' Passing for something means appearing to be it in other people's eyes. It is about the impression he makes, rather than physically going past someone.
Non.
'No.' A brief negative reply can stand on its own. Here it answers whether Gabriel knows the incident JoeyStarr is about to describe.
Elle n'avait pas son script avec elle.
'She didn't have her script with her.' The past form of have describes the situation at that time. The word for her appears again after with, referring back to Julie.
Alors moi, sympa, je lui donne le mien.
'So me, being nice, I give her mine.' The word for hers or his can also mean to her or to him before an action. Here it means to her; the final possessive means mine, standing in for my script.
Elle le prend comme un torchon sale! C'est agaçant.
'She takes it like a dirty rag! It's annoying.' The little word for it stands before takes. The dirty rag is a comparison that shows how insulting he found the gesture.
Non, ça va.
'No, it's fine.' The expression literally says that goes. With the short no in front, Gabriel is saying there is no problem with leaving the phone unanswered.
Réponds!
'Answer it!' This familiar instruction comes straight from the action answer. French can leave its object unstated when the ringing phone makes it obvious.
D'accord. J'ai rencontré cette fille.
'Okay. I met this girl.' The completed past introduces a new event: meeting someone. The word for this points to one particular woman he now wants to discuss.
Ce n'est pas mon genre. Elle est blonde, elle est normale!
'She's not my type. She's blonde, she's normal!' Type can refer to the kind of person someone is attracted to. The two descriptions that follow are feminine because he is describing a woman.
Mais je suis attiré par elle comme un aimant.
'But I'm drawn to her like a magnet.' The comparison uses like before magnet. The word meaning by introduces the person who attracts him, with the strong form of her after it.
Tu vois? C'est très puissant.
'You see? It's very powerful.' The short question checks whether the listener follows his explanation. Very strengthens the description powerful.
Mon inconscient et celui de Julie Gayet se heurtent de partout.

'My subconscious and Julie Gayet's clash everywhere.' The word meaning the one stands in for subconscious after Julie's name is introduced. The plural action says that the two inner worlds collide with each other. Now let's listen to the whole scene again from start to finish.
Dis-le si je t'ennuie.
Non, excuse-moi! Regarde, j'écoute. Vas-y, je suis tout à toi.
Je n'en ai plus envie maintenant.
Allez, j'écoute! Et alors?
Je passe pour un idiot! Tu sais ce qu'elle fait?
Non.
Elle n'avait pas son script avec elle.
Alors moi, sympa, je lui donne le mien.
Elle le prend comme un torchon sale! C'est agaçant.
Non, ça va.
Réponds!
D'accord. J'ai rencontré cette fille.
Ce n'est pas mon genre. Elle est blonde, elle est normale!
Mais je suis attiré par elle comme un aimant.
Tu vois? C'est très puissant.
Mon inconscient et celui de Julie Gayet se heurtent de partout.

Gabriel describes an attraction he cannot explain, and JoeyStarr applies the idea to his own clashes with Julie. Listen again for the expressions about giving attention and being drawn to someone. See you next time.
Bonne soirée!
